newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo army discuss 1997 military budget-agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugo army discuss 1997 military budget-agency.

text.p: The Yugoslav supreme defence council discussed army financing in 1997 at a meeting held in Belgrade on Thursday, Yugoslav news agency Tanjug said.
"The council reviewed basic elements of the 1997 military budget," the agency quoted the country's presidental military cabinet statement.

"In keeping with the 1997 economic policy to maintain monetary stability through intensive economic growth, the council took the view that realistic financial possibilities existed of improving army's combat readiness to enable it to exercise its constitutional powers," the report said.

The report gave no details on the size of the military budget, nor the percentage it will account for in the government expenditure. In 1996 the military budget accounted for 74 percent, or 4.21 billion dinars ($842 million), half percent down against previous year.
The army said it was 1.22 billion dinars ($244 million) short of the ammount needed for performing its defence duties.
The government's planned 1996 budget was set at 5.89 billion dinars ($1.17 billion).
